To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

•Character-based neural models outperform word-based models on a wide range of tasks, •The best results can be obtained by jointly learning word and character representations, and •Character representations can be learned from raw text, with no additional annotations.
•The use of character-level information improves the performance of sequence labelers, especially for rare words, by learning a richer representation of the words.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of sequence labeling, and in particular, with how we can use the rich linguistic information available in the characters of a word to improve the performance of a state-of-the-art neural sequence labeling model.
the problem of learning to predict the syntactic function of a word from the surrounding context.
the following question: How can we improve the state of the art for sequence labeling?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach of incorporating character information into a neural sequence labeling model is able to improve performance on a number of NLP tasks.
the neural network models have shown to be more accurate than the traditional machine learning methods.
the LSTM model is a good model for sequence labeling tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the character-level information can be effectively integrated into the word embeddings to boost the performance of neural sequence labeling models, without increasing the model capacity.
, we can use character-level representations in neural sequence labelers and it would help improve the performance.
we propose a simple yet effective method to improve the performance of neural network models for sequence labeling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
character information can be useful in many NLP tasks.
the performance of a neural network can be improved significantly when it is trained to attend to character-level features.
character-based models can improve sequence labeling performance on out-of-domain text, even if the character-based models are not trained on any in-domain data.
